in_text_mentions: Ophthalmic examination: All patients underwent a fundoscopic examination including slit lamp and indirect (90 and 20 diopter lenses, respectively) ophthalmoscopy following dilatation of the pupil using 1% tropic amide. For suspected cases of retinal pigment epithelium and differentiation with other pigmentation, Coherence tomography was used. Color fundus photographs were obtained to document the number and size of CHRPE lesions when possible (Figure 2).

plate_findings.evidence: Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium appears hyperpigmented
fish-tail depigmentation at one margin of the lesion

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Binocular retinal fundus photographs (patient II-17) showing hyperpigmented CHRPE lesions with the characteristic fish-tail depigmentation at one margin; caption explicitly attributes the hyperpigmented lesion to CHRPE. B: Binocular retinal fundus photographs (patient IV-13) with hyperpigmented CHRPE lesion and fish-tail depigmentation at the margin; disease attribution given directly in the caption. C: Fundus photograph (patient III-1) of a hypopigmented CHRPE lesion with fish-tail depigmentation at one margin; caption attributes the lesion to CHRPE. Hypopigmented CHRPE is a recognized less common form. D: Fundus photograph (patient IV-2) of a hypopigmented CHRPE lesion with fish-tail depigmentation at one margin; caption attributes the lesion to CHRPE. E: Fundus photograph (patient IV-13) of a hypopigmented CHRPE lesion with fish-tail depigmentation at one margin and a hyperpigmented halo; caption explicitly names CHRPE. The...
panels.attribution_text: Carvalho et al. Use of congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium as a clinical sign of familial adenomatous polyposis.. Arquivos brasileiros de oftalmologia 2024. doi:10.5935/0004-2749.2023-0115. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Retinal fundus images of study participants that were obtained via digital retinography. A, B) Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium appears hyperpigmented, with fish-tail depigmentation at one margin of the lesion (patients II-17 and IV-13, respectively in the family pedigree). C, D) Congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium appears hypopigmented, with fish-tail depigmentation at one margin of the lesion (patients III-1 and IV-2, respectively in the family pedigree). E) congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium appears hypopigmented, with fish-tail depigmentation at one margin of the lesion and a hyperpigmented halo (patient IV-13 in the family pedigree).
in_text_mentions: ged from 1 to 4 and that in the left eye ranged from 1 to 3. The total number of lesions in both eyes ranged from 2 to 6 regardless of age. The lesions varied in size from punctate (dot) lesions (Figure 3) to lesions measuring 0.25-4 disk diameters. Except for the dot lesions, all other lesions were oval in shape. Fish-tail depigmentation at one margin of the lesion was observed in all the patients (Figure 4). Variation in the pigmentation within the lesions was also noted. In one patient, computed tomography (CT) was performed to differentiate the CHRPE-type lesion from a melanoma (Figure 5).

plate_findings.evidence: multiple pigmented, flat lesions, of different sizes

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Color fundus photograph (right eye) of a 33-year-old woman showing multiple flat, well-demarcated hyperpigmented retinal lesions in a grouped pattern, consistent with CHRPE as described in the caption and text. [raw subtype: grouped/multifocal CHRPE] B: Color fundus photograph (left eye) of the same patient with bilateral multiple flat, well-delimited hyperpigmented retinal lesions matching the captioned CHRPE lesions. [raw subtype: grouped/multifocal CHRPE] C: Fundus autofluorescence image (right eye) of the same patient showing multiple well-demarcated hypoautofluorescent lesions corresponding to the captioned pigmented, flat CHRPE lesions. [raw subtype: grouped/multifocal CHRPE] D: Fundus autofluorescence image (left eye) of the same patient showing bilateral multiple well-demarcated hypoautofluorescent lesions consistent with the captioned flat pigmented CHRPE lesions. [raw subtype: grouped/multifocal CHRPE]

in_text_mentions: 0-year-old healthy female, with no relevant ophthalmology history either. She presented a CDVA of 20/ 20 in both eyes; normal biomicroscopy and PIO measurement; and a fundoscopy with a hyperpigmented lesion, minimally elevated, with well-defined margins in the temporal region of the posterior pole in the left eye (Fig. 1 B). The third patient was a 33-year-old healthy woman, with no relevant ophthalmology history, a CDVA of 20/ 20 in both eyes, normal biomicroscopy and tonometry and a fundoscopy with retinal hyperpigmented lesions, multiple, round, well-delimited, flat, and bilateral (Fig. 2).
